statement.p: Compute the flux of the vector field \vec F = 4 x\vec i+ 4 y\vec j through the surface S, which is the part of the surface z=4 - (x^2+y^2) above the disk of radius 2 centered at the origin, oriented upward.

static.solution: S as z=f(x,y)=4 - x^2 - y^2, we have d\vec A = (-f_x\vec i -f_y\vec j + \vec k)dx\,dy. = (2x\vec i + 2y\vec j + \vec k)dx\,dy. Thus, \int_S\vec F\cdot d\vec A =\int_R 4(x\vec i+y\vec j)\cdot (2x\vec i+2y\vec j+\vec k)\,dx\,dy =\int_R 8(x^2+y^2)\,dx\,dy. Converting to polar coordinates, we have \mbox{flux} = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{2} 8 r^2\, r\,dr\,d\theta =(2\pi)(2)r^4\bigg|_0^{2} = 64\pi.
